Specification: This module specifies a tutorial version of binary search over an input sequence of integers, searching for a given key using machine-style integer bounds and returning either a matching index or a negative insertion-point encoding. The state consists of the current low and high bounds, a termination flag, and the returned value, with Init setting up the initial search interval and Next modeling one search step or stuttering after termination. The spec also defines a postcondition stating that once the algorithm has terminated, the return value is correct in the sense that it is nonnegative exactly when the key is found; the comments note this property is derived from the Java Arrays.binarySearch behavior.
IfThenElse: IF ~isTerminated THEN IF low <= high THEN LET mid == (low + high) \div 2 IN LET midVal == INPUT_SEQ[mid + 1] IN \\/\\ midVal < INPUT_KEY /\\ low' = mid + 1 /\\ UNCHANGED <<high, returnValue, isTerminated>> \\/\\ midVal > INPUT_KEY /\\ high' = mid -1 /\\ UNCHANGED <<low, returnValue, isTerminated>> \\/\\ midVal = INPUT_KEY /\\ returnValue' = mid /\\ isTerminated' = TRUE /\\ UNCHANGED <<low, high>> ELSE /\\ isTerminated' = TRUE /\\ returnValue' = -(low + 1) /\\ UNCHANGED <<low, high>> ELSE UNCHANGED <<low, high, returnValue, isTerminated>>

IF MatchingIndices /= {} THEN returnValue + 1 \in MatchingIndices ELSE returnValue < 0
